input.quote: IBM grants Customer a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement.
input.rationale: § 12.1 is the only grant clause. It is expressly "revocable" with no stated standard, so IBM may withdraw the licence at will — walk-away territory under the rule. It also names only Customer, with no coverage for Affiliates or Subcontractors acting on our behalf and no notice mechanic to add them, and § 14.17 confirms no other rights are granted by implication. The transferability limb of the fallback is satisfied by § 14.10, which permits assignment to a successor by merger, consolidation or acquisition, so we left that untouched. Redline makes the minimal fix: adds Affiliates and Subcontractors acting on our behalf, and limits revocation to termination for our uncured material breach.

proposal.summary: Extend the Base Components licence to Customer's Affiliates and Subcontractors and remove IBM's at-will revocation right
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended the Base Components licence to our Affiliates and to Subcontractors acting on our behalf, and replaced the at-will revocation right with revocation only on termination for our uncured material breach, so the licence cannot be pulled while we are paying for the Services. If helpful, we can accept affiliate coverage on written notice instead.

ops.oldText: IBM grants Customer a nonexclusive, revocable license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement.
ops.newText: IBM grants Customer, its Affiliates and its Subcontractors acting on Customer's behalf a nonexclusive license to use the Base Components solely in connection with the Services as provided under this Agreement. Such license is irrevocable during the term of the applicable Services, and may be revoked or terminated by IBM only upon termination of this Agreement or the applicable Service Option Attachment for Customer's uncured material breach.
